title: Cypress Medical — SOC 2 POC kickoff: acceptance criteria & security playbook
topics: SOC 2/ISO controls, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs, data retention
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 and ISO summary + compliance deck by 2025-10-17
Customer to send sample workload and 2-week traffic snapshot by 2025-10-20
Schedule in-env benchmark window (2 days) w/ SE & Cypress infra — target week of 2025-10-27
Follow-up call to finalize acceptance criteria on 2025-10-22
action_items: Lena Park: Send SOC 2 summary, ISO doc links, and pilot pricing sheet (due 2025-10-17)
Sofia Nguyen: Provide SAML metadata and IdP test account (due 2025-10-20)
Tom Ellis: Export 14-day traffic sample, example payloads, and max request size (due 2025-10-20)
Mateo Cruz: Draft benchmark plan and scripts for load/latency tests (due 2025-10-24)
summary: Kickoff for a 4-week POC focused on measuring inference latency and throughput for Cypress Medical’s triage assistant, with SOC 2 and SSO requirements gating production. Agreement on acceptance criteria, timeline, and next steps to run an in-environment benchmark and demo RBAC/audit logging flows.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I think we're good to get started — this is the Redwood POC kickoff for Cypress Medical. I'm Lena, AE. Mateo and Priya from the SE team are here to scope benchmarks and the security playbook.
[00:12] Dr. Amir Patel: Thanks, Lena. Quick intros — I'm Amir, lead on ML for the triage assistant. Sofia handles security and Tom owns platform. Lina is product.
[00:23] Lena Park: Great. High level: goals for today are to align on success criteria, what data/workloads you'll share, and the security controls we need for the pilot (SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs). Also set timeline for the two-day benchmark window.
[00:36] Mateo Cruz: Quick note from our side on scope — we want to test both latency (p50/p95) under your burst patterns, and steady-state throughput with KV cache warmup. Sometimes we call that K-V cash in notes — sorry, bad habit from transcribers.
[00:50] Sofia Nguyen: On SOC 2: can you confirm Redwood has an attestation and which trust services categories? We need to map to our vendor risk questionnaire.
[00:58] Lena Park: Yes — Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II covering security and availability. We also have ISO 27001 summary and some controls around encryption at rest and in transit. I'll send the deck.
[01:06] Dr. Amir Patel: For acceptance, our bar is strict: we need p95 inference latency under 350ms for typical 512-token prompts at our target QPS of 6 sustained, 20 bursts; throughput should maintain at least 80% of baseline on concurrent requests. Also, we need no PII exposure and audit trails for all inference calls.
[01:24] Mate o Cruz (sic): Right, so clarify — when you say 512 tokens, do you mean input plus expected generation or input only?
[01:30] Lina Garcia: Input plus expected generation, about 512 total. Average response length ~120 tokens but worst-case up to 600.
[01:39] Mateo Cruz: That matters because it affects memory and KV cache usage. For benchmarks we'll run sequence-length sweeps: 128/256/512/600 to hit those tails.
[01:48] Tom Ellis: Our infra constraints: private VPC, no egress of raw payload to third-party storage, logs must be shipped to our SIEM (Splunk) and we want SAML SSO. Will Redwood private deployment support that for a short pilot?
[02:01] Priya Desai: We have a Private deployment option that can run in customer VPC or via our Private hosted offering. For the pilot we recommend sandbox in your VPC using our lightweight control plane with customer-managed networking — that satisfies the egress control and gives you SAML.
[02:15] Sofia Nguyen: We need RBAC to ensure only the ML team can create models and only platform can change network config. Does Redwood support attribute-based roles or just pre-set roles?
[02:24] Mateo Cruz: We support RBAC with role templates and custom roles. You can map SAML attributes to groups; you can restrict actions like deploy, rollback, and view logs. We also emit audit logs with user-id and action.
[02:36] Sofia Nguyen: How granular are those logs — do they include model hash, version, and full request/response payload? We can't have responses landing in logs if they contain PHI.
[02:45] Lena Park: By default audit logs include metadata — user, action, model id, timestamp. Full payload logging is optional and can be disabled; for PCI/PHI use cases customers opt out of payload logging and we provide hash references and request IDs.
[02:58] Dr. Amir Patel: Good. For compliance we also need key management: can we integrate our KMS?
[03:04] Priya Desai: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. For hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer keys in some cases — but for the pilot, VPC + customer KMS is recommended.
[03:14] Lena Park: Let’s capture acceptance criteria draft so we're aligned: 1) p95 latency < 350ms for 512 tokens at 6 QPS sustained, 2) throughput holds at expected concurrency with no error rate >1%, 3) integration with their SAML IdP for SSO and group mapping, 4) RBAC enforced and audit logs flowing to Splunk with no raw responses, 5) SOC 2 evidence provided. Any additions?
[03:33] Tom Ellis: Add retention policy on logs — we need 1 year of audit trail.
[03:36] Sofia Nguyen: Also, need an incident response contact and support SLA for the pilot window.
[03:40] Lena Park: We can provide a dedicated SE on-call during the benchmark window and escalation contact. SLA for pilot support is best-effort, written in the pilot addendum; we'll capture that.
[03:50] Mateo Cruz: On benchmarks — we'll need access to a representative sandbox environment. Ideally, you provide a k8s cluster credentials or we can deploy an agent in your VPC. For consistent results, we recommend we run the load from within your region to avoid cross-region network noise.
[04:05] Tom Ellis: We prefer you deploy an agent container in our cluster. We'll provide a test namespace and service account.
[04:12] Mateo Cruz: Perfect. For sizing: based on what you said (6 sustained QPS, peaks to 20) and 512 tokens, our rough estimate is a single XPU instance of the model at N-something quantization should handle baseline, but we will confirm after seeing real payloads. If you expect 600-token tails frequently we'll likely need an extra replica or burst capacity.
[04:32] Dr. Amir Patel: Budget-wise we can commit to a 4-week pilot with reserved capacity for the test days, but we need cost estimates. Lena?
[04:40] Lena Park: I'll include a pilot pricing sheet showing reserved capacity for two benchmark days plus hosted/private deployment line items.
[04:46] Sofia Nguyen: On legal/comms: we need a DPA and a noise-free NDA addendum for PHI handling. Who owns that?
[04:53] Lena Park: Our legal team uses a standard DPA and we can add an addendum for PHI handling for the pilot. I'll loop in legal after the call.
[05:00] Lina Garcia: Timeline — we want the end-to-end pilot in 4 weeks. Ideally benchmark in week 2, then analysis and follow-up in week 3, and decision by end of week 4. Is that realistic?
[05:09] Mateo Cruz: Yes, with prompt sharing and infra access this is doable. Typical timeline we propose: prep week (collect artifacts), deploy & run benchmarks (2 days) in week 2, evaluation & tweaks early week 3, acceptance review end week 3. But we'll match your 4-week plan.
[05:24] Lena Park: Let's lock dates: today is Oct 15, so prep items due Oct 20, benchmark week Oct 27, follow-up analysis Nov 3, decision Nov 7.
[05:34] Tom Ellis: Works for us. A few technical clarifications — model variants: do you handle automatic fallback between a higher-capacity model and cheaper quantized variant if latency spikes?
[05:44] Priya Desai: We support model routing policies: you can set primary model and fallback variants. For the pilot we'll test both fixed-route and fallback to ensure graceful degradation.
[05:54] Sofia Nguyen: For SAML mapping — we need to map 'platform-admin' and 'ml-editor' groups. Can Redwood map arbitrary group names from our IdP?
[06:02] Mateo Cruz: Yes, you can map SAML group attributes to our role templates. We'll walk through the mapping during integration.
[06:08] Dr. Amir Patel: A couple of gotchas from prior POCs: warm start vs cold start matters — please log cold-start latency separately.
[06:15] Mateo Cruz: Good point. We'll capture cold-start metric (first inference post-deploy) and steady-state after warmup.
[06:20] Lina Garcia: And request sampling — we want simulated PHI to test redaction + to ensure no raw responses in logs.
[06:26] Priya Desai: We can run redaction tests. For the pilot we'll validate that logs do not contain responses and that if payloads are retained we can apply customer-side redaction rules.
[06:36] Lena Park: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO summary and pilot pricing, Mateo will send the benchmark plan, customer provides SAML metadata and traffic samples, and we'll schedule the in-VPC agent deploy window.
[06:50] Dr. Amir Patel: One more ask — we need a short runbook for the benchmark days so our on-call infra engineer knows what to expect.
[06:57] Mateo Cruz: We'll produce a runbook with steps, expected traffic profiles, rollback plan and contact list.
[07:03] Sofia Nguyen: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:06] Lena Park: Nothing from us. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and calendar invites for the benchmark.
[07:12] Tom Ellis: Thanks.
[07:13] End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors (Mateo/Mate o), and shorthand (KV cache -> K-V cash) — original audio had slight overlap during the SAML discussion.
